_comment: wallpapers.com, described 2026-10-16 from the site as it answers from this machine. The `www` host
301s to the apex, so the apex is what is used everywhere here.
ROBOTS: /robots.txt is 28 Disallow lines under `User-agent: *`. Two of them shape this file:
`/search` (so ask=false - there is no text box for this site) and `/download/`, which is where the
site's real 4K/5K/8K originals live behind rel="nofollow". Those are NOT taken. What robots leaves
open is /images/hd/<key>.jpg, and that is the biggest file this description will ask for.
WHAT THE LISTING ACTUALLY SAYS: each card is <li class="content-card horizontal|vertical"> around
a <figure class="detail-data" data-type="wallpaper" data-key="KEY" data-title="..."> whose <img
src> is /images/thumbnail/KEY.jpg. The full-size file is not in the page: it is /images/hd/KEY.jpg,
built from the same key - measured on three keys: 117145, 419731 and 183218 bytes, all 200, with
the app's own UA (a Chrome UA gives byte-identical answers, so the UA is not checked).
/images/high/KEY.jpg is the same picture at a 900 px long edge (34797, 36732, 54849 bytes) and is
what the hero takes: the big pane is 1360 px wide, so 900 upscales 1.5x instead of the 300 px
cover's 4.5x, and one card preview costs 40 KB rather than 400 KB of originals.
/images/hd4/ and /images/hd8/ are md5-identical aliases of /images/hd/ - bigger names, same bytes.
THE 59 AND THE 60: the page carries 60 data-key attributes but only 59 data-type="wallpaper"; the
extra ones are the header's 'Top Coloring' JSON blob (coloring-pages/thumbnails/<n>_<n>.jpg) and
one each of svg/png/pictures/backgrounds. Anchoring the record on data-type="wallpaper" is what
keeps those out - measured 59 records, 59 distinct .jpg thumbnails, and the thumbnail's basename
equal to the key in all 59.
PAGING is a query (`?p=N`), and the page prints its own window of page links, so last_page is read
as the max of \?p=(\d+)" on the page: /4k says 53, /nature 201, /abstract 71, /space 35, /anime-4k
15. Asking past the last page does not 404 - /4k?p=54 comes back byte-identical to page 1 - so the
arrows must never be allowed to walk past what the page itself printed.
NO SIZE ON THE CARD: the file's own resolution is unpredictable (600x900 through 2160x3840 in six
samples) and the listing does not print it, so `size` is deliberately absent. The card shows no
resolution rather than a guessed one; the manifest gets the real numbers from the file itself.
CATEGORIES: the site's nav carries 113 of them. Six are listed below - each one measured to return
cards through this record (41-60) and to page with ?p=. /car was dropped: it renders 60 cards but
prints no ?p= links at all, so its pager would be a lie.
